children: Tamboran delivered first gas to the Northern Territory market in September 2026 and reported a pro forma cash position of approximately US$240 million at June 30, 2026. The company completed construction of the Sturt Plateau Compression Facility on time and under budget and executed the largest stimulation campaign in the Beetaloo Basin. Tamboran also completed strategic transactions and financing actions during the 12 months, including a ~US$300 million capital raise and acquisition of Falcon Oil & Gas.
Pro forma cash balance of approximately US$240 million at June 30, 2026 (reported cash US$231 million less restricted share; pro forma includes US$15 million receivable from acreage sale).
Reported cash balance of US$225 million at June 30, 2026 (noting restricted cash adjustments referenced).
Drawn debt of US$30 million (net to Tamboran) related to SPCF construction as of June 30, 2026, with additional undrawn infrastructure debt noted.
Completed a public offering in April 2026 raising US$186 million net of fees.
First gas deliveries to the Northern Territory commenced in September 2026; SPCF production ramping with contracted 40 TJ/d to the Northern Territory Government and SPCF capacity of ~50 TJ/d.
Completed Sturt Plateau Compression Facility construction on time and approximately US$9 million below P50 cost forecast; commissioning activities expected to complete in 4Q 2026.

Executed the largest stimulation campaign in the Beetaloo Basin with 178 stages across ~30,000 lateral feet, including successful deployment of locally sourced Beetaloo Red Sand in 10 stages and zipper-frac operations achieving up to 12 stages in a day.

Drilling activity: completed initial two wells of a three-well SS1 pad program (record lateral drilling speed), and commenced a two-well campaign on Santos-operated EP 161; planned further stimulation and mid-2027 BCDA drilling with DWE/INPEX.

Strategic moves: Final Investment Decision (FID) on Shenandoah South Pilot Project, acquisition of Falcon Oil & Gas, farmouts and JV arrangements (including with DWE/INPEX and Santos), and secured infrastructure debt partially backstopped by the Northern Territory Government.

title: Tamboran reports first gas deliveries, strengthens cash position with ~$240M — 4Q FY26 update
